Regex Hardening & Architecture Refactoring - The NEW file resolves ReDoS by eliminating catastrophic backtracking in query processing. First, it hardens numeric regular expressions—replacing overlapping optional quantifiers like \d*\.?\d+ with non-ambiguous patterns like (\d+|\d+\.\d+|\.\d+) to prevent exponential matching paths on malformed inputs. Second, it decouples parsing from execution. The OLD version used an inefficient string-slicing backtracking loop (doMatch/find) that repeatedly evaluated regexes against substrings. The NEW version delegates query parsing to a dedicated, safer parser (parseWithoutCache) and caches results, preventing execution-phase ReDoS attacks entirely

uses 3rd party library - The code imports and uses the RE2 library (`const RE2 = require('re2');`) and passes it into `urlRegex(RE2)`. RE2 is a linear-time regular expression engine that avoids catastrophic backtracking by design. By using RE2 instead of the native JavaScript regex engine for URL-related matching, the code mitigates ReDoS risks even when processing user-controlled input, since RE2 enforces predictable, non-exponential runtime behavior for regex evaluation.

input validation - The new implementation strengthens Git URL handling by centralizing protocol definitions and parsing through dedicated fromUrl and parseUrl modules. Supported protocols are explicitly mapped in #protocols, including SSH, HTTP, HTTPS, and Git-specific variants, reducing reliance on loosely interpreted URL schemes. It also uses the standard URL API in unknownHostedUrl() to safely extract and reconstruct hostname and pathname components instead of manually parsing URLs with complex regular expressions. input validation + regex hardening : The fix strengthens the regular expressions used to parse CSS color values. In the older version, numeric patterns were relatively permissive and allowed optional signs and decimal representations in ways that could lead to inconsistent or unexpected parsing behavior. The updated version uses more explicit numeric patterns and requires commas between RGB, RGBA, HSL, and HSLA components. Additionally, the new implementation introduces centralized clamping functions (clampi, clampt, clampa, and clamph) to constrain color components and opacity to valid ranges before formatting. These changes make parsing and output handling more predictable, enforce stricter input validation, and reduce ambiguity when processing malformed or unusual color values.
